title: A new generation of effective core potentials: Selected heavy 5d and 6p elements
abstract: We expand the correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) library by developing semi-local pseudopotentials and matching basis sets by heavy-elements from $5d$ (Hf, Os, Hg) and $6p$ (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. In order to accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin-orbit coupling, and electron-electron correlation, we implement a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy across three distinct resolutions. This includes a small 60-core (Hf, Os, Hg) that explicitly correlates subvalence shells, a large 78-core definition for the main-group elements that rigorously accounts for core polarization and relaxation effects in sparse valence environments, and an intermediate 68-core partition for Hg and Tl. This 68-core architecture represents a unique development in the ccECP library, optimizing the balance between accuracy and computational efficiency in a manner unexplored for ligther elements. Optimized against relativistic all-electron CCSD(T) references, the ccECPs deliver outstanding atomic precision, achieving a global average atomic low-lying states deviation of just 0.045 eV. This accuracy translates directly to robust molecular transferability, systematically restricting dissociation energy discrepancies to under 0.03 eV, equilibrium bond lengths to within 0.005 Å. By enforcing a regularized, finite potential at the origin for enhanced numerical stability in stochastic quantum Monte Carlo methods, this library removes a critical methodological bottleneck for predictive many-body simulations of heavy-element systems and materials.
summary: This work introduces a new generation of correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) specifically designed for heavy 5d and 6p elements. By employing a sophisticated, tiered core-valence partitioning strategy and optimizing against high-level $	ext{CCSD}(	ext{T})$ calculations, the potentials achieve exceptional accuracy and transferability. This advancement removes a major bottleneck for predictive simulations in heavy-element materials science.
main_problem: The development of highly accurate and transferable effective core potentials (ccECPs) for heavy elements (5d and 6p blocks) to correctly model electronic structure.
main_result: The new ccECPs achieve outstanding atomic precision (0.045 eV deviation) and robust molecular transferability (dissociation energy errors < 0.03 eV), overcoming limitations in modeling heavy-element systems.
method: The potentials are derived by optimizing parameters against high-fidelity all-electron benchmarks calculated using $	ext{CCSD}(	ext{T})$ theory, incorporating a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy.
model_or_system: The focus is on heavy elements from the 5d (Hf, Os, Hg) and 6p (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. The underlying theory involves partitioning the semi-local SO relativistic ECP ($	ext{SOREP}$) into scalar and spin-orbit components.
key_observables: Global average atomic low-lying states deviation (0.045 eV), dissociation energy discrepancies (< 0.03 eV), and equilibrium bond lengths (< 0.005 Å).
important_parameters: The core-valence partitioning uses three resolutions: 60-core, 78-core, and 68-core, optimizing the balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that core-valence correlation effects can be systematically captured through the tiered partitioning strategy, and the optimization relies on $	ext{CCSD}(	ext{T})$ reference data.
figures_summary: Figures compare Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD), Low-Lying Mean Absolute Deviation (LMAD), and Weighted Mean Absolute Deviation (WMAD) of the new ECPs against all-electron references.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework for the ccECPs, outlines the tiered partitioning strategy, describes the optimization process using various objective functions, and presents benchmark comparisons demonstrating superior accuracy and transferability.
why_interesting: The rigorous treatment of relativistic effects and the development of highly accurate, transferable potentials are crucial for any advanced many-body simulation involving heavy elements, which is a key area of condensed matter and quantum chemistry.

The vertical dashed lines mark the equilibrium bond length (Re) extracted from the AE reference and ccECP.
